_comment: THE NUMBERS IN THIS FILE ARE CONSERVATIVE AND UNVALIDATED, exactly as in
config/governor.json. BRIEF.md fixes no threshold and CLAUDE.md rule 8
forbids inventing one and then treating it as decided, so every value here
exists so that a threshold EXISTS, is committed, and can be changed in a
commit that says why.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored by the
loader. Every other key under dashboard is required: there is no built-in
default and the dashboard refuses to draw on one.
windowMs is how far back the page reaches: the outcome counts it shows
and the price series it draws are both taken over this window. Seven
days, because a household watching a few dozen listings sees a handful
of observations per listing per week and a shorter window would draw a
series with one mark in it.
timeZone is the IANA zone every instant on the page is shown in, and it
is shown BESIDE the instant: a page that showed bare local times would
be read differently by the same person in two seasons.
outputPath is where the page is written, relative to the repository
root. Its directory has to exist: the command refuses to create one,
because a page written somewhere nobody expected is a page nobody reads.
stalenessCeilingMs is how old a source's newest SUCCESSFUL request may
be before the source reads as broken. The roadmap phase's fail-safe is
that a source with no recent successful fetch reads as broken and not
as quiet, and this is the number that decides 'recent'.
A source with no entry here has its health REFUSED by name rather than
measured against a ceiling nobody chose. That is deliberate: adding a
source is where its ceiling gets decided.
bestbuy-api collects on a daily cadence, so 48 hours is two missed runs
- long enough that one skipped day is not an alarm, short enough that a
dead credential is visible the next time the owner opens the page.
jsonld-generic and alert-channel have no adapter and no deliveries yet,
so neither has ever had a successful request and both read as broken.
That is the honest answer: nothing has proved they work.
